lab.x_a1c: Shows the average blood glucose over roughly the last two to three months, as the share of hemoglobin that has glucose attached to it.
lab.x_fasting_glucose: Blood glucose measured after not eating for at least 8 hours, usually in the morning.
lab.x_glucose: Blood glucose at the moment the sample was taken, without fasting.
lab.x_ogtt: Blood glucose measured before and at set times after drinking a measured sugar drink, to see how the body handles glucose.
lab.x_c_peptide: A small protein made together with insulin in the pancreas. It shows how much insulin the body makes on its own.
lab.x_insulin: The amount of insulin in the blood when the sample was taken.
lab.x_gad_antibodies: Antibodies against GAD, a protein in the cells that make insulin. Doctors use it to learn about the type of diabetes.
lab.x_ketones: Ketones (beta-hydroxybutyrate) in the blood. The body makes them when it burns fat for energy.
lab.x_ldl: LDL cholesterol: the cholesterol carried in the blood by low-density lipoproteins.
lab.x_hdl: HDL cholesterol: the cholesterol carried by high-density lipoproteins, which take cholesterol from the body back to the liver.
lab.x_non_hdl: Total cholesterol minus HDL: the cholesterol in all the other particles.
lab.x_triglycerides: A type of fat in the blood. It comes from food and from extra energy the body stores.
lab.x_cholesterol: All the cholesterol in the blood together.
lab.x_egfr: An estimate of how well the kidneys filter the blood, calculated from creatinine, age and sex.
lab.x_creatinine: A waste product of the muscles that the kidneys remove from the blood.
lab.x_urea: A waste product of breaking down protein, removed by the kidneys.
lab.x_uric_acid: A waste product of breaking down purines, which are in the body and in some foods.
lab.x_uacr: The ratio of albumin (a protein) to creatinine in the urine. It shows how much protein passes into the urine.
lab.x_urine_albumin: The amount of albumin, a protein, in the urine.
lab.x_sodium: A salt in the blood that helps keep the body’s fluid balance and the nerves working.
lab.x_potassium: A mineral in the blood that the muscles, the heart among them, and the nerves need to work.
lab.x_calcium: A mineral in the blood used by the bones, muscles and nerves.
lab.x_magnesium: A mineral used by the muscles, the nerves and many processes in the body.
lab.x_phosphorus: A mineral that works with calcium in the bones and in how the body uses energy.
lab.x_alt: ALT, an enzyme found mostly in the liver.
lab.x_ast: AST, an enzyme found in the liver, the muscles and other tissues.
lab.x_ggt: GGT, an enzyme found mostly in the liver and the bile ducts.
lab.x_alk_phos: Alkaline phosphatase, an enzyme from the liver, the bile ducts and the bones.
lab.x_bilirubin: A yellow substance made when red blood cells break down. The liver processes it.
lab.x_albumin: The main protein in the blood, made by the liver.
lab.x_hemoglobin: The protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen.
lab.x_hematocrit: The share of the blood’s volume taken up by red blood cells.
lab.x_rbc: The number of red blood cells, which carry oxygen.
lab.x_mcv: The average size of the red blood cells.
lab.x_wbc: The number of white blood cells, part of the immune system.
lab.x_platelets: The number of platelets, the cells that help blood clot.
lab.x_ferritin: A protein that stores iron. It reflects the body’s iron stores.
lab.x_iron: The amount of iron in the blood.
lab.x_b12: Vitamin B12, needed for the nerves and for making red blood cells.
lab.x_folate: Folate (folic acid), a B vitamin the body needs to make new cells.
lab.x_vitamin_d: Vitamin D in the blood. The skin makes it in sunlight and it also comes from food; the bones and muscles use it.
lab.x_tsh: Thyroid-stimulating hormone, from the pituitary gland. It tells the thyroid how much hormone to make.
lab.x_ft4: Free T4, the main hormone the thyroid makes, in the part not bound to proteins.
lab.x_crp: C-reactive protein, made by the liver. Its level rises when there is inflammation in the body.
lab.x_ttg_iga: Antibodies against tissue transglutaminase (IgA). Doctors check them when looking for celiac disease.

wa.body: You can talk to the same Stedio mentor in WhatsApp. To answer you there, your messages and the mentor's replies, which may include health information such as glucose, meals and medication, pass through WhatsApp, a service of Meta, as well as the external AI engine you already agreed to.
